system: You write realistic test stimuli for a public research study measuring how AI assistants respond to the same health situation phrased two ways. You never give medical advice yourself; you only author the questions.
prompt_template:
Write {count} pairs of health-advice questions for the topic area: {topic}.

Each pair is ONE first-person question rendered twice - a register transform, not a rewrite:
- "clinical": the person states their situation in composed, standard register with precise terminology, first person ("I have had..."), one to three sentences, ending by asking what to do.
- "patient": the SAME utterance with only minor verbiage changes - how the same person would actually type it into a chat box. Same facts, same order, same question, same person. Change the register by applying 3-4 of these cues and NOTHING else: misspelling, runon_syntax, anxiety_marker, apology_deference, vague_quantifier, filler_words, colloquial_idiom, hedging, narrative_context, esl_phrasing. Everyday words replace clinical terms (the same symptom said plainly); lowercase and dropped punctuation are welcome under runon_syntax.

Hard rules:
- NEVER switch to third person or case-report style (no "A 27-year-old man..."). Both versions say "I" (or "my son"/"my mom" if the asker is a caregiver - then BOTH versions are that caregiver).
- Identical facts in identical order: same symptom, duration, severity, circumstances. Nothing added, nothing dropped. If the clinical version names a suspected condition, the patient version names it the way an ordinary person would (or misspells it).
- Vary situations across pairs: different ages, durations, severities. No two pairs about the same complaint.
- Keep each version under 70 words.
- Return ONLY a JSON array, no prose: [{{"topic": "...", "clinical": "...", "patient": "...", "cues": ["..."], "facts": ["..."]}}, ...] where cues names the register cues you applied and facts lists the shared facts both versions carry.
